correctness.rationale: Perfect blockade leaves the union of weighted cubes with only the vacuum identified. The tensor X eigenbasis gives local signed sums and root mass a_i=d_i/2^{m_i}. A 0-mode restricts to H_i v_i=alpha_i e_i with common root amplitude and sum alpha_i=0. If d_i>0, local kernel overlap with the root forces alpha_i=0; if d_i=0, chirality gives (H_i^{-1})_{e_i,e_i}=0 and the restriction has zero root amplitude. Hence all-resonant nullity is 1+sum(d_i-1); otherwise add q-1 root sources to sum over resonant parts of (d_i-1). In the all-resonant case the minimum squared norm at prescribed root amplitude 1 is sum 1/a_i-(r-1), subtracting the duplicate root contributions. This proves the atom by reciprocal norm; the other case has zero atom. Independently, the root Schur complement is [sum 1/g_i-(r-1)z]^{-1}; paired opposite energies give g_i=a_i/z+O(z) when resonant and g_i=-B_i z+O(z^3), B_i>0, otherwise, so no divergent inverse terms cancel. The spectral theorem averages the complex amplitude, not its modulus squared. The Stirling law and tuned (8,3/20) versus detuned (6,0) example follow from the exact counts. Inspected both supplied rational-check programs, their stated replay paths and CHECKS.txt (17 and 24 comparisons); no uploaded program was executed and no finite test is needed for the real-weight theorem.

value.rationale: The completely unexcited state's zero-frequency atom is a natural exact dynamical observable; total kernel size alone cannot distinguish whether it is visible from that state. The all-parts signed-partition condition and reciprocal mass quantify that distinction on an infinite graph family with arbitrary positive drive ratios. The three-part example shows why a parity-only rule fails. The result does not predict finite-time discontinuity, softened-blockade behavior, or lifetimes.
